Yosef Nimni, son of Kalima and Vitorio, was born on 28 Cheshvan 5691 (19 November 1930) in Tripoli, Libya.

Yosef grew up in Tripoli, studied at the Petro Burri elementary school and at a local high school. In his youth he was a member of the youth movement in his city.

In 1948 he immigrated to the Land of Israel from Tripoli, via Italy, as part of the illegal immigration (Ha'apala). These were the days of the War of Independence, and he immediately enlisted and served in the Golani and Alexandroni Brigades.

After his discharge he worked from 1951 to 1956 at the Public Works Department (today Israel Roads). Alongside his work he completed three years of study at the "Shalosh" vocational school in the automotive mechanics track and a year of study in automotive electrics, took a variety of professional courses, and served as chief mechanic and as a vehicle inspector.

In 1953 Yosef married Miriam. The couple made their home in Ramat Gan, and they had three sons: Avigdor, Uri and Yigal.

In 1956 he joined the General Security Service (Shin Bet). He worked as a mechanic, as a work manager in the maintenance department, and as a work manager in the operations vehicle and garage. He worked in the Shin Bet for many years with loyalty, and invested many hours in various assistance tasks for his colleagues.

After retiring, between 1995 and 1997, he volunteered in the printing section of the logistics headquarters.

Yosef Nimni passed away on 9 Adar 5759 (25 February 1999), at the age of sixty-nine. He was laid to rest in the Yarkon cemetery in Tel Aviv. He is survived by his wife, three sons and siblings.
